question: When are property taxes due, and how do I pay them?

nuggets.text: The local governing body sets the due dates by ordinance.
nuggets.quote: The governing body may also by ordinance establish due dates for the payment of local taxes; may provide that payment be made in a single installment or in two equal installments; may offer options, which may include coupon books and payroll deductions, which allow the taxpayer to determine whether to pay the tangible

nuggets.text: The late-payment penalty is capped at 10 percent of the tax.
nuggets.quote: No penalty for failure to pay a tax or installment shall exceed (1) 10 percent of the tax past due on such property;

nuggets.text: Interest starts the day after the due date, at up to 10 percent a year.
nuggets.quote: Interest may commence not earlier than the first day following the day such taxes are due by ordinance to be filed, at a rate not to exceed 10 percent per year.

nuggets.text: The City Treasurer bills and collects.
Charlottesville real estate tax is due in two installments (June 5 and December 5).
nuggets.quote: Real estate tax is due in two equal halves on June 5 and December 5. Personal property (vehicle) tax is also due in two installments on June 5 and December 5, and the June 5 installment includes the city vehicle license fee. nuggets.text: Bills can be paid through the city's InvoiceCloud payment portal.
nuggets.quote: The Treasurer must mail bills at least 14 days before the due date, and may choose not to mail a bill of $20 or less. You can choose paperless bills and email reminders in the city's InvoiceCloud payment portal. The city's penalty policy says not receiving a bill is no excuse for paying late, so if no bill arrives, contact the Treasurer's Office before the due date.
